term:Ground Truth.deep_dive: The reference answers a supervised model learns from and is scored against — labels, verified outcomes, gold standards. Its quality caps everything: label errors become learned errors, and labeler bias becomes model bias, which is why annotation guidelines, inter-annotator agreement, and label audits are governance controls rather than technical trivia.
term:Ground Truth.exam_tip: Trace bias to labels, not just features — 'the historical decisions used as ground truth were themselves biased' is a recurring scenario key.

term:Impact Assessment.deep_dive: The genus of look-before-you-leap instruments: structured evaluation of a system's potential effects before and during deployment — with species including DPIAs (GDPR, personal data), AIIAs (broad AI impacts), FRIAs (EU AI Act fundamental rights), and algorithmic impact assessments (public sector). Shared anatomy: describe, identify stakeholders, assess severity × likelihood, mitigate, document, revisit.
term:Impact Assessment.exam_tip: Match the species to the trigger: personal data high-risk → DPIA; high-risk AI deployer (public body) → FRIA; general AI ethics → AIIA.

term:Incident Management.deep_dive: The discipline of handling AI failures in production: multi-channel detection, pre-authorized containment (rollback, kill switch), root-cause investigation, remediation, obligation-driven disclosure (AI Act serious incidents, GDPR breaches, sector regulators), and institutionalized lessons. AI adds novel incident species — bias events, drift failures, prompt-injection compromises — to the classic catalog.
term:Incident Management.exam_tip: Order is tested: detect → contain → investigate → remediate → disclose → learn; skipping containment or disclosure is the planted error.

term:Integration Testing.deep_dive: Verifying the model works inside the assembled system — data pipelines feeding it, APIs serving it, interfaces presenting it, workflows consuming it. A fair model in a system whose UI amplifies bias, or whose pipeline silently reformats inputs, still produces harm — integration is where component-level assurance meets system-level truth.
term:Integration Testing.exam_tip: The recurring scenario: model tests clean, system behaves badly — integration testing (and system-level fairness evaluation) is the missing control.

term:Issue Management.deep_dive: The tracking discipline for problems below incident severity: logged, owned, prioritized, remediated, and trended — bugs, degradations, complaints, near-misses. Its governance value is the pipeline: issue trends are the early-warning system that catches incidents while they're still issues.
term:Issue Management.exam_tip: Issues are managed continuously; incidents trigger response protocols — the severity threshold between them should be predefined.

term:Life Cycle.deep_dive: The governed arc of an AI system — ISO 22989's stages run inception → design & development → verification & validation → deployment → operation & monitoring → re-evaluation → retirement. Lifecycle thinking is the spine of every framework: obligations, documentation, and risk work attach stage by stage, cradle to grave.
term:Life Cycle.exam_tip: Governance is lifecycle-long — any answer implying it ends at deployment ('we validated it before launch') is structurally wrong.

term:Localization Policy.deep_dive: Rules requiring data to be stored or processed within a jurisdiction — motivated by sovereignty, surveillance, and enforcement concerns (Russia, China localization laws; EU data-residency preferences). For AI it constrains architecture: training pipelines, cloud regions, and inference endpoints must respect where data may live.
term:Localization Policy.exam_tip: Localization is the inverse of free transfer — where transfers can't be legitimized, keeping data in-jurisdiction is the compliance path.

term:MITRE ATLAS.deep_dive: The adversarial-ML threat knowledge base — ATT&CK's AI sibling: a matrix of real-world attack tactics and techniques against AI systems (poisoning, evasion, model theft, prompt injection) with case studies. Used to structure AI threat modeling, red-team planning, and security-control mapping.
term:MITRE ATLAS.exam_tip: ATLAS = adversarial threat catalog for AI security — distinct from risk frameworks (RMF) and management standards (42001).

term:Maintenance Schedule.deep_dive: The planned cadence of AI upkeep: model retraining windows, data refresh cycles, dependency patching, performance reviews, and documentation updates — turning 'we'll retrain when it breaks' into governed, budgeted operations with owners.
term:Maintenance Schedule.exam_tip: Predefined maintenance beats reactive maintenance in every scenario — models decay on schedule, so upkeep should run on one too.

term:Manufacturing Defect.deep_dive: The product-liability theory for units deviating from their intended design — the flawed copy, not the flawed blueprint. For AI it's the awkward fit among the three theories (software replicates perfectly), which is why design defect and failure-to-warn carry most algorithmic liability weight.
term:Manufacturing Defect.exam_tip: Manufacturing = deviation from design; design = the design itself is dangerous; warning = known risks uncommunicated — classify the fact pattern.
